A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same CAX paper. The main sections, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison. V1's Appendix B is genuinely absent from v2, rather than unavailable through extraction.

before.justification: V1 reports original CAX speed benchmarks, neural cellular automata simulations, MNIST reconstructions, and 1D-ARC accuracies in Section 3.2.1 and Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains the original CAX benchmarks and neural cellular automata results, including the authors' 1D-ARC results alongside GPT-4 scores attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The perceive/update architecture, controllable inputs, JAX scan procedure, and three proposed NCA experiments remain unchanged. The added Section 3.1 paragraph explains existing architectural flexibility without introducing a new component. Appendix changes concern experimental configurations.

E1.justification: The same cellular automata simulations, growing and diffusing NCA examples, MNIST tasks, and 18 1D-ARC task types are retained. The revised grid and channel sizes do not establish different datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain CellPyLib for classical simulations, TensorFlow implementations for NCA training, growing NCA for regeneration, and the cited GPT-4 direct-grid results for 1D-ARC. Newly cited architectural approaches are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes diffusion steps from 128 to 64 in Table 3. Table 5 changes the 1D-ARC grid length from 128 to 96, channels from 32 to 64, and steps from 128 to 64. These revise configurations within the retained evaluation design; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The damage-and-regeneration comparison in Figure 5, MNIST reconstruction examples, and 1D-ARC case visualizations are retained. No ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test, or error analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Removing Appendix B removes its explicit seed = 0 for the example notebook. Figure 3's error bars remain unchanged, and neither version supplies their run counts or statistical definition. This is a limited loss of seed disclosure, not evidence of changed experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Figure 3's benchmark results, all Table 2 task accuracies, and the qualitative results in Figures 4–8 are unchanged. Table 2 still reports 60.12% for NCA and 41.56% for GPT-4. The revised appendix settings do not establish a new performance result or a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The CA and controllable-CA definitions and local/global update rules in Sections 2.1–2.2 are mathematically unchanged. Reversing the sides of the state-update equalities is equivalent notation. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a flexible, hardware-accelerated CA library, support across CA types and dimensions, speedups up to 2,000 times, three novel experiments, and NCA performance exceeding GPT-4 on 1D-ARC. Abstract edits do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: The regeneration and attractor explanations, MNIST information-bottleneck interpretation, and discussion of NCA failures on odd-even and size-comparison tasks remain unchanged. The added architecture paragraph elaborates the existing controllable-input and modularity rationale without substantively revising the scientific interpretations or limitations.

D1.justification: V2 removes Appendix B's complete growing-NCA training example, including target preparation, initialization, loss, pool updates, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and 8,192-step training loop. This substantially reduces implementation detail within the PDF. Appendix A revises hyperparameters and repository references are consolidated; the public repository was already linked in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds Pajouheshgar et al. (2023), Grattarola et al. (2021), and Tesfaldet et al. (2022), expanding the introduction's context on convolutional, graph, and attention-based NCA architectures. The central positioning relative to existing CA libraries remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the abstract and introduction, adds an architectural explanation and acknowledgments, expands Appendix A's introduction, and makes small language corrections. Appendix B is removed, but the main section sequence and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 splits the author block, restyles the code boxes, adjusts Figure 2's caption, and changes Appendix A's table headings, rules, and captions. The notebook appendix disappears. Figures 1–8 and the principal result-table displays otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves architectural exposition and related-work context but removes the worked training notebook, reducing self-contained implementation guidance. Tables 3 and 5 also change settings while the reported outcomes remain identical; the PDFs do not establish whether these changes correct documentation or describe different experiments. These mixed documentation effects and unresolved setting corrections prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
